intro: A Chicago post-punk quartet, angular and quick.
story: Deeper is a Chicago post-punk quartet of Nic Gohl, Drew McBride, Shiraz Bhatti and Kevin Fairbairn, whose self-titled debut came out on Fire Talk in 2018. Auto-Pain followed on Fire Talk in early 2020. In July 2022 they played the Pitchfork Music Festival in Chicago, and Pickathon that summer. Careful!, their Sub Pop debut, followed, and Pitchfork said it opens the band to something almost like joy.
artist_reel_line: Careful! was their Sub Pop debut.

intro: A Los Angeles psychedelic rock band, loud and quick.
story: Frankie and the Witch Fingers formed in Bloomington, Indiana, and moved to Los Angeles in 2014; Permanent Records issued their second album in 2015. ZAM came out in 2019, and Monsters Eating People Eating Monsters... on Greenway and RAS on October 2, 2020, which Clash praised as groovy, momentous garage-rock refinement. They played Pickathon in 2022. Data Doom followed in 2023, and in June 2025 the studio album Trash Classic.
artist_reel_line: Monsters Eating People Eating Monsters... came out on October 2, 2020.

intro: A Southern California indie band with a hypnotic groove.
story: Inner Wave is a Los Angeles psychedelic indie band with Pablo Sotelo on lead vocals and guitar. Apoptosis came out in early 2022, and they toured it that year, with Coachella on both weekends, Outside Lands, Pickathon and a December run supporting Foals.

Mariachi Tradición is an audition-based mariachi ensemble at Forest Grove High School in Oregon, started by Lesslie Nuñez; 2025 marked its 10th anniversary. They played Pickathon in 2022, and have opened for La Santa Cecilia and George Lopez in Portland and played the Oregon Symphony. A 10th anniversary concert with Las Cafeteras was set for May 31, 2025, at the Reser, and in September 2026 they took the stage at the fifth El Festival de Mariachi in Hillsboro.

MØTRIK is a Portland krautrock band formed in 2012, with Erik Golts, Cord Amato, Lee Ritter, Jonah Nolde and Dave Fulton. They recorded a session for Pickathon's Edge series in 2022 and played the farm the next year. MØØN: The Cosmic Electrics of MØTRIK came out in 2021 and their fourth album, EARTH, on Jealous Butcher Records on November 7, 2025; OPB's Think Out Loud featured them on December 1.

intro: A Brooklyn synth-pop group, playful and strange.
story: Operator Music Band is a Brooklyn art-pop group with analog synthesizers, motorik beats and waves of feedback. Live for Live Music said they carried the festival with deep, danceable grooves when they played Pickathon in 2022. Their latest record, the EP Four Singles, came out in March 2024.

intro: A singer and songwriter out of The Deslondes.
story: Riley Downing is a Missouri singer-songwriter and a co-lead voice of the New Orleans group The Deslondes; he met Sam Doores at Woodyfest. His solo debut, Start It Over, came out on New West on May 14, 2021, and the Deslondes record Ways and Means on July 8, 2022, the summer of his Pickathon set. He once worked as a garbage man in rural Missouri, which inspired the later Landfill Poetry, his second solo album, on Oh Boy Records, the label John Prine started, in August 2026.
artist_reel_line: His second solo album, Landfill Poetry, came out on Oh Boy in August 2026.

story: The Onlies are an old-time string band of Sami Braman, Riley Calcagno, Vivian Leva and Leo Shannon, friends who grew up in Seattle and Lexington, Virginia; Leva joined in 2017. Their self-titled fourth full-length was their first as a quartet. They played Pickathon in 2022 and again in 2026, and You Climb the Mountain came out in 2025.

intro: An old-time duo from Durham, now Viv and Riley.
story: Vivian Leva and Riley Calcagno came back to Pickathon in 2022, three years after their first visit, a year after their self-titled album came out on Free Dirt, produced by Joel Savoy, and with Leva's Time Is Everything from 2018 behind them. They toured the UK festivals that May and June. Imaginary People followed on Free Dirt in September 2023, a sound grown into lush indie-folk. They perform now as Viv and Riley, out of Durham, North Carolina, and in October 2026 they played a session for WYSO radio.
